Cherenkov emission by radiotherapy beams is an intrinsic and non-ionizing radiation that has been characterized by simulation, and that has been detected and imaged by a novel CCD spectrometer system, and that can be NIR-shifted by CdSe/Zn quantum dots, and that can potentially provide superior image quality to MV imaging for low-density-variety and low-optical- attenuation materials, and that can also be used to simultaneously acquire dosimetric and functional tumor oxygenation signals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to detect Cherenkov emission from high energy radiation beams, we are able to shift the Cherenkov emission into the NIR window of tissue where it is more detectable, we are able compare the Cherenkov images with MV imaging, we are able show a significant contrast in Cherenkov images over MV images and we are able to show that Cherenkov imaging is linear with dose.
Cherenkov emission by high-energy radiation therapy beams is a potentially viable tool for online imaging, with the added benefit that Cherenkov radiation is intrinsic to the treatment beam.
Cherenkov emission is a potential tool for online imaging of radiotherapy beams and can be NIR-shifted to increase its detection efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CE can be used for online imaging in radiotherapy, and that the NIR shift can be achieved by QD-based CE imaging.

CE by high-energy radiation beams can be detected with high sensitivity, NIR-shifted for improved detection, and applied for online imaging in radiation therapy, yielding image quality superior or at least competitive with MV imaging.

CE is a promising tool for online radiotherapy imaging, since it is intrinsic to the radiation beam, non-ionizing and can be NIR-shifted with QDs to improve detectability, potentially offering image quality superior to conventional MV imaging.
